failure_hypothesis.hutch_response: Schema v60 persists stable event intent before append acknowledgment, restores pending records after process restart, and commits canonical event plus outbox deletion atomically. A unique event key prevents duplicate recovery across two Store instances and conflicts on payload reuse.
failure_hypothesis.reported_or_reproduced: Reproduced: an accepted append held only in the process-local queue disappeared after os._exit before the asynchronous writer committed it.
failure_hypothesis.source_version_date: Hutch schema before event-outbox migration, observed 2026-10-11

observations: The serialized event/migration suite passed its existing greater-than-1,000 events/second gate. A first throughput run while three pytest processes shared the host measured 874 and failed; the isolated rerun and later serialized suite passed.
Historical schema rows remain unchanged; the v60 migration is idempotent. The interrupted 56-to-current migration rolls back and retries with the outbox table and event-key index present.
The tests cover process termination and SQLite restart, not OS power loss or physical filesystem failure.
This store-only slice changes no rendered UI and has no new screenshot; responsive Studio and marketing visual captures remain separate evidence.
